Complete Empirical Research Plan: “Teacher Impacts on Student Achievement”

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) / randomized assignment of teachers to classrooms, implemented through a linear regression with classroom-teacher fixed effects (a “within-experiment value-added” design).  
Why appropriate: Because teachers are randomly allocated within grade-school-year cells, treatment status (the identity or pre-measured quality of the teacher) is orthogonal to student ability and other confounders. A simple comparison of means is unbiased; regression adds precision and allows covariate adjustment and teacher heterogeneity analysis.

Optional extension: Split-sample value-added (VA). Use data from cohorts t-2 and t-1 to form an out-of-sample VA score for each teacher; treat assignment to a “high-VA” teacher as the experimental treatment.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable: D_i = 1 if student i is assigned to a teacher whose pre-estimated VA (from earlier cohorts) lies in the top tercile of the distribution; 0 otherwise.

Control group: Students randomly assigned to teachers in the bottom two terciles (or, in robustness checks, to the bottom tercile only).

Treatment timing: The treatment occurs in the academic year in which the teacher is assigned (t). Outcome (end-of-year standardized score) is measured at t and possibly at t+1, t+2 for persistence.

No running variable → not an RDD.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Random assignment integrity: teacher–class matches are truly random within school-grade-year cells.  
Plausibility: Administrative lotteries documented by the district; baseline covariate balance can be tested.

A2. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): A student’s outcome depends only on her own teacher, not classmates’ teachers.  
Plausibility: Reasonable because classes are separate; threat if students interact across classes during pull-outs or recess.

A3. No selective attrition correlated with treatment: test-taking and enrollment at year-end do not differ systematically by teacher assignment.  
Plausibility: District’s compulsory testing lowers risk; must be empirically checked.

A4. Correct measurement of VA: the pre-estimated teacher VA measure is unbiased for true teacher quality.  
Plausibility: Achieved through large pre-sample and shrinkage (Empirical Bayes).

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Non-compliance (administrators override random draws).  
Remedy: Verify compliance logs; use random assignment as an instrument for actual teacher received (two-stage least squares).

T2. Differential attrition / missing test scores.  
Remedy: Show attrition balance; bound estimates (Lee bounds); inverse probability weighting.

T3. Classroom spillovers (e.g., high-quality teacher influences peer learning that spills to control group through recess interactions).  
Remedy: Include peer-teacher-quality composition controls; cluster SEs at grade-school to absorb common shocks; sensitivity tests excluding schools with high cross-class interaction.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # regressions with high-dim FE
library(AER)          # ivreg for robustness
library(lmtest); library(sandwich)

# 1. Load & merge ----------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("student_teacher_panel.csv")   # assume tidy long panel

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
# Standardize test scores within grade*year for comparability
dt[, zscore := scale(test_score), by = .(grade, year)]

# Teacher value-added from past cohorts (pre-computed & merged)
# high_VA = top tercile indicator
tercile_cut <- quantile(dt[pre_sample == 1, teacher_VA], probs = c(1/3, 2/3))
dt[, high_VA := fifelse(teacher_VA >= tercile_cut[2], 1L, 0L)]

# Main treatment dummy (only for experimental years)
dt[, treat := high_VA * experimental_year]

# 3. Main specification ----------------------------------------------------
# Student i in class c with teacher j, school s, grade g, year t
# FE: school*grade*year to soak up common shocks
reg_main <- feols(zscore ~ treat + baseline_score + gender + race_eth +
                  lunch_status | school^grade^year ,
                  data = dt[experimental_year == 1],
                  cluster = ~teacher_id)

summary(reg_main)

# 4. IV robustness: random draw as instrument for actual teacher -----------
# random_draw_highVA is a binary flag from the lottery
iv_est <- ivreg(zscore ~ treat + baseline_score + gender + race_eth +
                lunch_status | random_draw_highVA + baseline_score +
                gender + race_eth + lunch_status,
                data = dt[experimental_year == 1])

coeftest(iv_est, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = ~teacher_id)

# 5. Balance check ---------------------------------------------------------
bal_vars <- c("baseline_score", "gender", "race_eth", "lunch_status")
lapply(bal_vars, function(v){
  feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ treat")), data = dt[experimental_year == 1])
})

# 6. Attrition robustness --------------------------------------------------
# IPW example
dt[, prob_obs := mean(!is.na(zscore)), by = .(treat)]
reg_ipw <- feols(zscore ~ treat | school^grade^year ,
                 data = dt[experimental_year == 1],
                 weights = ~1/prob_obs,
                 cluster = ~teacher_id)
summary(reg_ipw)
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Economic theory and previous quasi-experimental evidence (e.g., Chetty et al.) suggest that a 1 SD increase in teacher VA raises contemporaneous math/reading scores by ≈ 0.10–0.15 SD. Therefore, moving from bottom-two-terciles to top tercile (≈ 0.67 SD in VA) should lift scores by roughly 0.07–0.10 SD. Direction: positive.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RCT)
-------------------------------------------------
C1: Successful randomization verified (balance) ............................ 1  
C2: Low and non-differential attrition ..................................... 0.5  
C3: No interference/SUTVA holds ............................................ 0.5  
C4: Treatment delivered as designed (high compliance) ...................... 1  
C5: Outcome measurement not affected by treatment (same test) .............. 1  

Average score: 4 / 5 → evidence supports causal interpretation but spillovers and attrition warrant care.

-------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
